formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

selections.rationale: Fix one attributed responsibility on the configuration path and run a first direct check for it. Reading Raft.appendConfigurationEntry shows that the leader publishes a new configuration through setLatestConfiguration(configuration, future.Index()), recomputes the commitment voter set and restarts replication after dispatchLogs, without inspecting the dispatch outcome; dispatchLogs assigns the index and pushes the future before StoreLogs and, on a StoreLogs error, answers the future and steps down to Follower. The obligation is therefore that a server must not treat a configuration as its latest unless the entry was durably stored, and the check drives exactly that path with one injected durable-write failure.

Review the executed direct check for the configuration-durability obligation. The clean-copy run completed the selected test (exit 0) and reported the discriminating pair: the admitted configuration-append attempt saw a single-voter, index-2 log (pre_voter_count=1, pre_log_last_index=2), and after the injected durable-write failure the node reported store_failed=true with latest_voter_count=2, latest_index=3, committed_index=1 and log_last_index=2. formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.
